raw_comment:
.  More than half of  teens who answered this survey use SNS such as YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram every day. Especially, the rate of YouTube is the highest rate of all. In fact, I often watch YouTube for too many hours on weekends. In addition, leaders of various countries have concerns about negative influences SNS can have on teens. So, some of them have started to limit its use by teens in their countries. 
2. I wonder why teens depend on SNS. I often use SNS in my free time, but I haven’t clearly understood what makes SNS so attractive yet. Also, I wonder why the rate of Facebook is lowest of all. 
3. If SNS becomes widespread in my community, it will be hard for teens to focus on studying and club activities. Plus, wrong information spreads throughout my community rapidly. Then, teens will accept it without doubting if it’s right and get in trouble on the internet. 
4. Reconsider Your Interactions with SNS!

raw_comment:
I am a father of four adult sons the youngest of whom is 21.  All of them have some level of disdain for the world as they find my generation has left it for them to deal with (can't blame them). All of them grew up in parallel with the ever more ubiquitous presence of tech and social media. 

Based on this very small sample size, I wonder if teens and young adults give any thought to how much their views and opinions are influenced by corporate behemoths who have been using AI for some time with the express intent of drawing them every more deeply in a facsimile of the world that is not real and sometimes dangerous. 

What generation might realize the influence of corporate behemoths that are behind these platforms and reject them outright? 

For users of all ages, when will we stop being lab rats for these companies that monetize our eyeballs with no regard to the negative impacts on society?

Have there been any studies on the degree to which kids would say they are more influenced by their social media platforms or some social media "influencer" than they are their parents? I can't imagine being a parent today trying to instill values to my children.

When will Facebook go out of business given the younger generations are not using it? Can't wait for that!

raw_comment:
Thank you for providing this interactive platform, it is a great community service.

Wondered if you had seen this:
Kaiser Family Foundation:https://www.kff.org/other/video/video-profiles-of-generation.  

Shocking portrait from 2010 when used to engage parents in discussing this with their teens and middle school children.

As a Women’s Health NP with extensive teen population,in rural underserved community, all impoverished, and all had phones!!!
2010! Yikes, the tsunami was coming.
 
Thanks for this opportunity to respond.
Aloha

It can also affect their school work since most teens scroll on their phone during class, not paying attention.

raw_comment:
I notice that YouTube, a social media platform with a lot less features related to communication (such as private messaging) compared to other social media software, appears to be the most popular platform in term of how often teenagers use it. I wonder if this is because of how content on YouTube differs from other places; instead of only allowing short videos, it focuses on longer videos, and said videos are more likely ones that a user can keep on in the background instead of being something they actively have to focus on. I myself use YouTube several times a day--I don't even use the other social media platforms used in this graph for one reason or another. 

"The Trends of Trends: Where do Teens Spend their Time Online?"

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I have noticed that YouTube is the most watched social media platform and I believe that TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram would have all taken that spot but somehow YouTube blew them out of the water. 
2. What do you wonder?
I wonder how YouTube did that because I always see people on Snapchat, Instagram, and TikTok but not YouTube. I mostly use it for educational purposes and I'm confused and intrigued how it overtook the other, more popular apps. I also wonder how diverse the study was in demographics, home life, etc… 
3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
The constant use of social media has been affecting the young population immensely over the past decade and the problems are starting to show. Depression and ADHD have been proven to be directly influenced by social media and many other problems are showing up as time goes by. It is creating a less communicative and more sheltered within their phone generation. My generation has a lot to do to fix the problems created by the generations before us and if we are holed up with our phones and social media these problems won’t be solved. 
4. What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
The graph shows how each of the different social media are used and their frequency of use by today's teenagers.
“Social media: the addiction of the century.”

raw_comment: Teenagers use social media platforms as a means of communication, self-expression, entertainment, and staying updated with current trends. They connect with friends, share personal experiences, engage with content creators, and join online communities. The benefits of life online for teenagers include increased connectivity with others, access to a vast amount of information, opportunities for self-expression and creativity, and the potential for finding support and community. However, there are also risks associated with life online, such as cyberbullying, privacy concerns, negative impact on mental health, addiction, exposure to online predators, and the distortion of reality through idealized portrayals. It is crucial for teenagers to be aware of these risks, practice responsible digital behavior, and engage in open communication with trusted adults to ensure a positive and safe online experience.

raw_comment:
I notice first the YouTube is the platform most used by teenagers, which is completely expected because it has both the most content and longer form content that can be more engaging and serve a much larger catalogue of audiences. The opposite here is TikTok and Snapchat which generally have much shorter content and yet both are close to YouTube in terms of constant use. This suggests to me that there may be a crossover between the two groups who use all three platforms for the same shorter content, while YouTube has a broader appeal that TikTok does not.

I wonder how this could be further broken down by age groups, as I'd put good money on the few Facebook users being much older than the average TikTok or even Instagram user. I'd also want to know the reason why each person or demographic prefers their platform, as speculation can only get you so far.

In terms of myself and my community/family I can say I notice a difference in the type of content me and family consume on a daily basis. My brother, who is several years younger than me enjoys a lot of the same topics but watches them in much shorter forms, while my mother watches much different things than I do but in similar length.

A good title would be "The Online Fight for Attention" or something along those lines.

raw_comment:
- I notice that more teens say they use streaming platforms in comparison to social media platforms. Youtube and TitkTok are both apps that allow users to find videos that interest them, and open their eyes to new content on the internet. Snapchat and Instagram are more of connective-based apps in which users can interact with others and their posts. 
- I wonder why Facebook was added in the survey. I believed that since Facebook was created in the early 2000s, it is now a platform for older people rather than teenagers from 13-17 years of age. I believe that Twitter or Pinterest should have been added to the survey instead.
- This relates to my community because there are large percentages of teenagers that use these platforms, myself included. I think that if my school were to complete the survey, it would receive similar results to this conducted survey results.
- Stalking Social Media

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I noticed that the amount of teenagers who answered “almost constantly” for YouTube, TikTok, and Snapchat were all within a 5% range. 19% of teens said they use YouTube almost constantly, 16% said TikTok, and 15% Snapchat. Even though YouTube had the most teens using it, its percentage of teens who use it almost constantly was not significantly higher than the other top 2 choices. 


2. What do you wonder?
I wonder how Facebook seems to not have as big of an effect on teens even if it is offering some of the same things like reels, posts, friends, and stories as other apps. I wonder why it isn’t used by teens because there is no clear reason why less than 12% of teens use it several times a day yet it is so popular with older generations. 


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
I feel that social media can have both a positive and negative effect on teens in my community. It can help lift each other up and inspire teens, but also can have an addictive side. Teenagers have a clear problem of being on their phones too much due to this addiction. This causes focus problems for teenagers aswell and I notice it a lot in school and for myself too. Even at jobs in my community run by teenagers, I notice phones are an issue while working. 


4. What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
Teenage Social Media Addiction Uncovered

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?


What I noticed from the article, What's Going On In This Graph? I have observed that the most common social media app for teenagers is YouTube. 19% of teens use YouTube consistently throughout their day. On the flip side, Facebook is the least common social media platform for teens to use, where less than 8% use this app consistently. 


2. What do you wonder?


After looking at this graph, I wonder why teenagers are so dependent on social media sites? As a teenager myself, I can say I am always on social media- but what causes this addiction is my question. We are living in a world today that depends on our phones and apps so I expected these numbers to be so high on social media usage.


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?


This not only affects my community, but it affects the whole world. Every trend, newest brand, product, and news outlet is mainly going to be shown to the world via social media. Social media has shifted the world's “social norms”. Social media has set unrealistic standards for everyone, and as an outcome that will affect my community. 


4. What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

This graph shows the more used apps by teens and how connected we are to our devices. 

Catchy Headline: “Is YouTube the New Facebook? See why teens are drawn to newer apps.”

raw_comment:
Apps that have practically endless content and an algorithm that sets you up to get sucked in for hours have the highest usage. What I think is more alarming is the percentage of people who say they use any of these apps almost constantly, especially because it is overwhelmingly more likely than using the app more sparingly. 

Does this prove that the apps become addicting? If someone starts using the app one or two times a day, will it become an app that they use almost constantly? Or does it depend on the person? 

I find from my experience that it does build up with time: It starts as something where you just wanted something to do, but then you realize that you should stopped a while ago. And it’s hard to have restraint when you are being fed content that you are essentially guaranteed to like

raw_comment:
1) I notice that YouTube is by far used the most with only 5% of people not using it daily versus over 1/3 of the same in other social media. It surprised me that 41% of people don't use Snapchat daily.  When I think of a social media that my friends and I use every day, I immediately go to Snapchat because of all the texting we do through group chats. I am not surprised by the lack of Facebook use as most kids I know do not use it.
2) I wonder where and how this data was collected. I know that in many Spanish-speaking parts of the world, WhatsApp might be a more popular choice and maybe that is why we see a decrease in the other platforms. Because this data doesn't make me think of a traditional American high school, I wonder how the respondents were chosen, and if this is a global survey.
3) A study like this exposes the addiction that we all have to our phones. For better or worse, I believe that we have become reliant on technology, constant approval, communication, and access to the world around us. It does not surprise me at all on YouTube and TikTok because, as a generation, we have trained ourselves to enjoy this information-packed age of quick learning. This study paints the picture that we are abandoning older sites in favor of more fast-paced and content-filled ones.
4) "The Transition of Social Media"

raw_comment:
1. I first noticed that it is a stacked bar graph, which I also helped me finally understand how bar graphs work, which was a bonus. I also noticed that YouTube had the most use out of every other platform, which my classmates seemed confused by since they didn't feel like they use YouTube that much, and they are teens. They seemed to think that the others, except Facebook, would be used more often in our age because that is what they use more. 

2. I am wondering how old the people were that were tested because if it was mostly 13-year-olds or 19-year-olds, there would be different results with each.  I am also wondering what would happen if they added other programs like Spotify and Netflix, like we were talking about in class, since I know a lot of teenagers use those programs, even more as they are in their later teens. I am also wondering what this does for teens' mental health since it isn't just this time they are on screens because they use it for school work as well. 

3. This affects my community because my neighbors are just starting to get into their teenage years and they are already clinging to their electronics. I do know that our generation is highly on the internet, but this idea of our generation, including me, are online most of the day, it makes you wonder what technology is going to replace for us in the future. 

4. Catchy title:

                        Get off UR Phone!!

raw_comment: I was pretty surprised that Instagram was so low, it feels like so many people talk about it so constantly. I guess it’s not surprising that Youtube is number one, especially with the addition of Youtube shorts recently. To be honest, I think Youtube might start going downhill if it doesn’t get more original content soon. It feels like the most popular videos right now are all just the same gaming videos. All the good content moved to Youtube shorts, but now Youtube shorts are just a bunch of children trying to get big with trends. Overall, using Youtube just makes me feel either bored, down, or even mad. The algorithm will just constantly give you one type of video because you watched one video from that category slightly longer than usual. I wish I could just find a good Youtube documentary that’s 40 or 50 minutes long and just watch it. But that type of video just isn’t being made anymore.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I mainly noticed that YouTube is a platform that is frequently used by teenagers. The prevalence of podcasts on Youtube also seems to be useful in multitasking during work. This is a skill that teenagers have learned in facing the challenges of shortened attention spans that may have been caused by an excessive use of social media.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why children are becoming increasingly drawn to the internet and smart devices. The influence of the internet and minimal social reactions during a person's childhood seems to accelerate the process in which they mature. It is clear that growing up in a digitally connected environment has an impact on a child's childhood and their life in later years. The overwhelming amount of information we encounter in our interconnected world also contributes the accelerated process of maturation that most children who spend excessive time on they internet experience.

How does this relate to you and our community? 

I have a younger sister who- in comparison to me, is more in touch with the internet than I was when I was her age. This experience highlights the difference between children who were born into a time in which they were surrounded by smart devices and children who spent more time playing outside and doing other things that do not require smart device usage. 

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph's main idea.

Sparkle and Screens!

raw_comment:
1) I noticed that of all the social media platforms, Facebook is by far the least used by teens. While 50% of the teens that responded for each platform use it at least once a day, Facebook’s teen respondents are nowhere near that margin. In fact, 2/3 of the teens that were asked about using Facebook said they didn’t even use the platform, while the highest non-use rate for the other platforms was around 2/5 or less of the respondents.

2) I wonder what percentage of these teens are male and which are female. In other words, is there any correlation between a respondent’s gender and how active they are on certain social media platforms? What about across all platforms? Do males spend more time on social media than females? 

3) As something that connects all human beings, social media is one of the most powerful tools on planet Earth which can be used positively or negatively. Social media can cause both severe addiction problems in a community or be a flourishing well of knowledge for people to learn about something. As a teen, I have experienced both sides of the double-edged sword that is social media. Many times, I have found myself doom scrolling through various of these platforms while on the flip side, they have also helped me study or understand many topics in school.

4) This graph is displaying the percentage of teens that use a social media platform for a given amount of time.

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?


I noticed that the graphical display shows a significant difference between the teens who use YouTube and the teens who use TikTok. 19% of the kids surveyed said they use YouTube almost constantly compared to the 3% that said they use Facebook almost constantly. I also noticed how while YouTube has the highest usage of the social media platforms on this display, TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram are decently close, but Facebook has a significantly lower usage rate from the people in this survey. 


2. What do you wonder?


I wonder what some of the driving forces that allow social media platforms like YouTube and TikTok to have much higher usage rates than Facebook. I also wonder how this would be different if the group of people interviewed were in the age range of 25 - 30.


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?


Social media has a huge impact on teens throughout our community. Social media is something that has taken over our country with benefits and negatives. Access to information and communication is easier than ever, but they also constantly take over our lives. 


4. What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.


"Facebook to Youtube: Unraveling the Changing Social Scene"

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that YouTube is the platform most used both almost constantly and several times a day, and only 5% don't use it ever, while 67% don't use Facebook. TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram are all used less than YouTube but a lot more than Facebook. Also, while fewer people use Instagram almost constantly than Snapchat, more people do not use Snapchat at all than Instagram.

What do you wonder?
I wonder what the average age of teens asked this question was because it could have been different if more older teens were asked or if more younger teens were asked.

How does this relate to you and your community? 
This relates to me and my community because I know some people are only allowed to use YouTube, so that would explain why most people use it. Also, I have heard people say that they don't like Facebook, which could be a reason for the small number of people using it.

raw_comment:
What did I notice?
I noticed that the survey focused on teens who spoke either Spanish or English, likely indicating that the survey focused on North and South America/ the western hemisphere. Only 5 categories of social media were analyzed. Youtube was the most popular among teens. Youtube was launched in early 2005, close to the birth of the youngest age group (17 year olds), and has gained popularity since. TikTok was launched in 2018, and known for shorter content. 
What do I wonder?
I noticed that the survey was taken in April and May of  2024, and I wonder how numbers have changed since the pandemic, and how the rest of the world uses each platform. I also wonder how answers may have been biased, because this was a self-conducted survey.
How does this relate to you and your community?
I’ve noticed that TikTok, Youtube and other forms of social media have gained popularity in recent years. More conversations are centered around content from TikTok, Snapchat, and other social media that I don’t fully understand. Furthermore, news is able to spread even quicker than before, and I’ve noticed a shift in social culture.
What’s going on in this graph? Create a headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
This graph is displaying the distribution of generalized amounts of time teenagers spend on social media. A title would be 'Trending Now: How Much Time Teens Spend on Social Media'

The use of social media also affects the learning environment as students may be distracted by their phones. 

The graph depicts the percentage of teens who use different social media platforms for different amounts of time. 
Headline: Social Media Platforms Most Enjoyed by Teens

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
The initial thing that jumped out at me is that 33% of teens do not use TikTok. These are not the stereotypes that adults put on teens with social media. I was also surprised that only 5% of teens don’t use YouTube. 


2. What do you wonder?
I'm curious if YouTube will still have such an influence on teens in the future now that TikTok is becoming one of the most popular social media apps. YouTube has been around for a while and is used for people to post videos that everyone worldwide can see. TikTok has developed the same concept of people being able to post videos even up to ten minutes long for the audience on TikTok to see. The difference between the two is that you don’t have to interact while watching YouTube, but with TikTok, you do. I wonder how this will affect how popular the two apps become. 


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
Social media has such a big impact on the community as a whole. Social media is how kids, teens, and adults find out information, support causes, stay connected with friends and family, and share their lives. Social media has many good values if you know how to use it, but if you don’t, it could be detrimental to your view of yourself and social media. 


4. What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
How influential are social media platforms for teens?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
Teenagers in this generation rarely ever use Facebook. More than half of the teenagers who were surveyed use YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, and/or Instagram at least once each day.  

What do you wonder?
I wonder if the people who don’t use Facebook have even heard of Facebook. I wonder if the reason that YouTube is so popular in the survey is because it is kind of an outlier among the 5 platforms. 

What impact does this have on you and your community?
The impact this has on me and my community is that my current community is the demographic of teenagers that have been surveyed. Social media has taken over the teenage community. Based on the information given in this graph, my generation uses and/or loves using YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram. There is that outlier of people liking Facebook as well. The information shows that my generation is somewhat addicted to social media. With over 50% of people having used Snapchat and Instagram, they are subject to possible hate if they post pictures about themselves on the platform. YouTube is quite safe for teenagers unless they come under fire through the comments or videos. TikTok is the same way as YouTube, where it might not truly affect teenagers based on how much influence a teen tries to have on the platform.  

What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
YouTube has taken over as the most popular platform that teens use.

raw_comment:
I notice that of the teens interviewed, 95% of them use YouTube. Of those that do use YouTube 60% of them use it more than once each day. For Tik Tok however 33% of the sample don’t use Tik Tok. I also notice that those that use tik tok are more likely to use it constantly than those that use YouTube. However, those that use snap chat are more likely to use it constantly than those of any other platform.  Furthermore, more of the sample uses SnapChat at least once a day than those that use Instagram each day. Overall, comparison between apps is important to understand them.
I wonder the amount of time each day that the average user spends on each app. That would provide insight into which of these apps see the most use. I also wonder if many of the sample subjects use one app more than once a day, and if that impacts the amount of time spent on the other apps listed. I also wonder, of those sampled, how many use 2 apps or less, and how often they use those apps.
Many in my community use these apps for hours on end and complain that they do not have enough time to do homework. However that being said, I played in a band and we were able to substantially grow our following through our social media account. Social media browsing is a great tool, and a fun activity. 
This graph shows the percentage of people who use specific social media platforms, and how often they use them.
My Headline: What social media teens use, and how often they do

- **No faceting** or small multiples.

|---|---|---|

| Percentage of teens | Quantitative | Segment length/width along x-axis; percentage text labels inside segments |

- **Segment labels**: percentages printed inside bars
- **Category labels**: platform names on the left; frequency labels above the bars
raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?


I noticed that YouTube is the most used platform and that 77% go on YouTube at least once a day. I also noticed that Facebook only has 19% of teens using it at least once a day, which is significantly less than the amount of teens using YouTube and other social media platforms.


2. What do you wonder?


I wonder why so many people use YouTube. The graph says that 19% of teens are constantly on YouTube which was very surprising for me. I feel like I and most people I know rarely use YouTube so it surprises me that so many people use YouTube on a daily basis. I wonder if this survey was conducted in a specific spot in the country that uses YouTube more, so it may be swayed by that. 


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?


This impacts my community because so many people are constantly on their phones and using social media. This may be bad for mental health. It seems like a lot of people are constantly on social media, but it would be better for people to get out and communicate with their peers in person.

This graph shows the percentage of teens and how much they use each type of social media.

raw_comment:
Looking at the graph right away, I notice that the majority of teens use YouTube the most, compared to all of the other platforms. I see that there is a very small portion of teens who don’t use YouTube compared to the other sites. 
I wonder, in comparison to teens, if adults have around the same data- especially in terms of YouTube and TikTok, and would wonder how different the data showing Facebook usage would be. 
This graph relates to me because I think that I would answer the survey similar to others. I do use YouTube and TikTok considerably more than other sites, and am among those who don’t use Facebook. In my community, I don’t know of many other teens who have Facebook accounts either. 
A catchy headline that could relate to this graph could be “The Fall of Facebook” because eventually as these teens get older, Facebook users will continue to dial down.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

I notice that the apps being most used by teens are less of communication apps and more entertainment.  Also,not everyone who answered responses are taken into consideration. Those who did not answer were not shown, the population of students therefore would go down in the sample and it could dictate the validity of the results pictured on the graph. The greater the population the more accurate the data and the greater the range influencing what is seen on this graph. We don't know the population, so validation of the data may not always be true for all teens.

what do you wonder?
I wonder what the population size sampled was? Where was the data taken? What type of students took the survey? Was it a random sample or did bias play a role? Why do teens prefer entertainment apps over communication apps? 

How does this relate to you and your community?

Social media is taking over people's lives. It is a big problem affecting the brain. We need to try and persist in using it less for entertainment and more for educational uses as well as communication. We should live in the moment more and spend less time on the screens. It relates  to me in how I use social media a form of entertainment typically through scrolling Tik-Tok. I can help myself by taking a step back from the screens and doing other things to spark interest without the use of social media

I also noticed on the graph that FaceBook is vastly less popular than the other platforms. This is probably due to the platform being older than most of the individuals interviewed.

I would also wonder how other age groups would respond to this survey. This could help marketers reach their target audience more effectively and save money by avoiding ineffective methods.
The captivating abilities of social media.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
On the graph, I notice a similarity between the second to top three social media apps listed. This includes Instagram, TikTok, and Snapchat for which the usage per day is very similar. I also notice that Facebook is rarely used for teens between the ages of 13-17 year olds. Finally, even though it is similar to the rest, YouTube surpasses every social media app with the most usage.

What do you wonder?
One question I wonder is why YouTube is so high. Could it be related to the use of the app as an educational tool? Could it be for different purposes than the following social media apps? Why is there a relation between TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram but not YouTube? The final question I have is where these statistics are coming from. For example, people seem to use Snapchat more than the graph demonstrates.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This impacts the community in a very negative way.  Phones have been a very unhealthy problem throughout the years. I could also see the certain apps people use to the damage made to the user. I also believe this can negatively affect the student's ability to learn. Finally, the content they receive can hurt these students.

 “Social Media”- “The Damaging Consequences”

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
 
I’ve noticed that teens seem to use apps where videos are available much more than apps where you have to scroll and look at still images or text posts. Also on these apps, social interaction is less available

What do you wonder?

I wonder why teens have stopped using social media for actually socializing as much. For example, the only socialization you can do on YouTube is commenting on videos. On Facebook or Instagram, you can comment on photos, directly message people, make group chats or even actual groups for certain interests, and more.

How does this relate to you and your community?

This relates to me and my community because my community is made up of many teenagers going to school, whether middle school or high school. It is also made up of parents and grandparents who worry about their children and grandchildren. Teens aren’t nearly as interested in socialization as in years before, which can cause a great decline in mental health and support systems. As teens stay inside using these apps, they’re stuck inside and not interacting with one another: at least, not in person.

Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

Are Teens Really addicted to “Social” Media, or Just “Media?”

raw_comment:
Things I observed about the graph regarding usage of different social media platforms among teenagers are how longer forms of content like YouTube and TikTok are the most commonly used and how apps like Facebook and Instagram, which are just pictures or short videos are the least commonly used. 
I wonder if how outdated or old social media platforms are is a factor in how much teenagers use a platform. This trend is present in the graph except for YouTube, but Instagram and Facebook two platforms that are older than Snapchat and TikTok are at the bottom of the list, while TikTok is the second most popular social media platform among teenagers. 
I can relate to the data of this graph with how I spend my time on social media, how my friends spend their time on social media, and how my family spends their time on social media. Me and my friends, mostly teenagers, are avid users of TikTok and YouTube, especially when compared to Facebook. However, I know people like my parents if they were to take the survey their most used social media platform would be Facebook, which would be my least used social media platform. 
Has Meta Fallen off of the Social Media Throne?

raw_comment:
1- Notice: 
	The thing about using a website constantly is that you can only use that particular website; there’s no time for other social media platforms. If you review the numbers of people who do use the sites constantly, then they add up- meaning that there is a very high percentage of people who use media frequently- just on different platforms. 

2- Wonder: 
	What is the life cycle of a social media platform? In the early days, Facebook was the most popular. And then Instagram. And now Snapchat. What causes the decline? Is it adult infiltration of a site? What does that mean for our society, and how does that attribute to the stereotype of a teenager? 

3- Relations: 
	Someone I know recently got into trouble at home and at school for abuse of social media privileges. I’m not someone who’s on Youtube frequently, so it was rather shocking to see what has been made available to young people, and how destructive it can be. Especially when they have such open access. I really do believe that it is corrupting, but at the same time it’s a catch twenty two- the very thing that is eating teens from the inside out is the very thing that we’re told we enjoy. The thing that is necessary for popularity. 

4- The Modern Jurmungand? A Study on the Life Cycle of a Social Company.

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I noticed that all the kids who took this survey did not say that they use facebook constantly, but 22% of them use facebook several times a day and/or one time a day. I also noticed that the kids that use Youtube several times a day is equal to the amount of kids who don't use snapchat (41%), which was interesting to me as I thought snapchat would be the most popular. 


2. What do you wonder?
I wonder why facebook has no constant users. I think this could be because of an age stigma, that facebook is for “old” people. I also wonder how snapchat is not the most popular, as in my opinion it definitely is. 


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
The impact is that between 10% -around 20% of kids nowadays are constantly on these social media apps. This can lead to addictions, and doing less things in the real world.

“Addictions that are not talked about enough”

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I noticed that Facebook is extremely unpopular among teens, with two-thirds of teens claiming they don’t use the application. This makes sense because, in my community, I don’t believe any of my peers use Facebook. I was surprised that almost every teen uses YouTube and only 5% don’t.


2. What do you wonder?
I wonder how teens can manage to stay productive when some claim that they use these social media almost constantly. How many hours per day does “almost constantly” mean? Are these teens less productive than teens who don’t use social media as often? Since YouTube is used the most frequently is it having the worst effect on the minds of teens?


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
Social media has an impact on me and my community because almost every teenager uses it, and many believe teenagers use it too much. The data shows how some social media such as YouTube and TikTok are used very often by teenagers and I can see why this is true. Many students can’t stay off their phones in class or choose to watch TikTok instead of finishing their school work.


4. What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
The graph shows the intensity of usage of different social media by teenagers, suggesting which ones are the most popular and addicting. 
Headline: Social media is overtaking social interaction

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I notice that the most popular platform is Youtube by far with about 77% of teens stating they use the platform about once a day or more. TikTok followed close behind in second with 52%. Facebook is by far the least popular platform with only 19% of teens commenting they use it about once a day or more. 
2. What do you wonder?
I wonder why, with the popularity of TikTok, the proportion of teens who use the platform about once a day or more is only 57%. I wonder how, if this research was conducted now if the new proportion of TikTok teen users would compare to Youtube teen users. Facebook seems to be falling out of favor with younger users so if the research was conducted today, would it be smaller?
3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
This impacts my community because of the growing influence of social media on teen mental health. Many people who spend excessive amounts of time online may feel dissatisfied with themselves or their life. In addition, social media can be addictive. As the algorithms of these platforms become more and more specified to their user’s desire then it becomes more and more enticing to the user. 
4. What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
This graph is using a segmented bar graph by frequency. It is telling us how often teens believe they are on those given platforms by percentage. 
Catchy headline: 2022 Teens Tied Up in Youtube and TikTok

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
I notice that over half the kids in the survey use Youtube at least several times a day, with 19% of that being almost constantly. Tiktok and Snapchat have similar data where around 15%-16% of kids are using it constantly, with about an additional 30% of kids using it several times a day. Facebook is by far the least popular app among teenangers with 67% of kids not even using it.
2. What do you wonder?
	I wonder what appeal youtube has for teenagers that facebook lacks and why it is the most popular app being used. I also was surprised to see that youtube is used more than TikTok since I always assumed TikTok was the more popular app. I wonder how different this graph will look in 10 years from now.
3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
	This graph showed me that there is a large percentage of kids who are constantly on social media apps every day, and social media has shown to have negative effects on people's mental health. Addiction to social media and phone usage among kids and teens is taking a toll on communities since it's so time consuming and affecting people's mental health at young ages.
4. What’s going on in this graph? Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea. The graph is showing how much each teenager uses an app.
“The Effect Social Media Has On Teenagers”

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?


I noticed that YouTube is the favorite social media as teenagers admit to spending the most time out. Only 3% fewer people admitted to being on TikTok almost constantly throughout the day. This gap expands to 9%.




2. What do you wonder?


I wonder why people spend so much time on social media; I also wonder what effect that happens to the teenage brain when they consume social media. The last thing I wonder is what type of content these teenagers consume on social media.


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?


This graph has made me want to stop, or at least lower, the amount of social media I consume. This graph also makes me want to delete Facebook as I don’t really use it, and it looks like neither do any of my peers.

raw_comment:
1. 	I first noticed in the graph that at the top, YouTube was used several times a day or more by 60% of teens, while at the bottom, Facebook, was reported as not used by 67% of teens. This shows me that in our modern day, YouTube has become the most popular social media platform for teens, while Facebook has fallen to the bottom, often known for being used mostly by adults. 

2. From looking at this graphical display, I am left wondering how each of the social media platforms impacts the other's teen usage time. For example, there may have been a post on Instagram from a celebrity that drew teen user time that would have instead gone to other platforms that day. Have these social media platforms ever used each other to build on their teen usage time, in the form of collaborative events or advertising?

3. Teen social media usage time has a significant impact on my community. Across America, we have seen a decrease in teen mental health and a rise in teen's social ability. Many of my peers (including myself) struggle to focus during class or stay on topic when a teacher is giving a lesson. Social media has also forced extremely short attention spans and instant gratification on its users. 

4. Outside in nature with friends, no, inside on phones with friends, yes!

raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
	More than 50% of people who responded to the questions opened YouTube, Snapchat, and TikTok once a day. A majority of teenagers also don’t use Facebook, with 67% saying that they don’t use the platform. I also noticed that for TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat, the largest majority of people either use them several times a day or don’t use them at all.


2. What do you wonder?
	I wonder if the results have to do with the social media’s content algorithm or the abundance of short-form content. For example, YouTube has long been a major platform in the online entertainment space. Their algorithm has had years to develop and their development team is massive. TikTok is known for its algorithm bringing unique feeds to every person who uses it. YouTube and TikTok have thousands of videos of content, each with plenty of short-form content that is easily accessible. I want to know if they can use them constantly because of the short-form content or the diverse range of content.


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
	As a student, this means that a large majority of my classmates are inattentive. They are distracted by social media and are almost constantly using them. This is a detriment to the learning environment and the future of society. If they are unable to break free from the bad habits then they will fail to learn given the opportunity. This leads to more unhappy and less useful members of society.

4. in the comments

raw_comment:
I notice that Youtube is used significantly more than other social media platforms. Youtube has the highest percentage of teens who use it significantly, the highest percentage of teens who use it several times a day, and has the fewest percentage of teens who don’t use the platform. Another idea that I would also point out is that Snapchat, Instagram, and Tiktok all have similarities. Across the board, there are minor differences between the three platforms but not enough that I would classify them as drastically different compared to others. You could argue that Instagram isn’t as popular due to the relatively low percentages compared to Snapchat and Tiktok and you would be right in the fact that there is a five and six-point difference between Instagram and Snapchat and Tiktok. Facebook is by far the least used social media platform and more than sixty percent of participants are not using the platform at all.

One of the ideas that I tend to wonder about these numbers is if these trials were truly independent from one another meaning that when participants were selected for the survey, were they chosen at random? Yes, it does say that 1,316 teens participated in this survey which is most likely a viable sample size but we don’t know where these participants come from. By not having a random sample, this could introduce unwanted bias into the survey.

1. What do you notice?
I notice that the percentage for teenagers that use Youtube almost constantly or several times today is almost equivalent to the percentage of teenagers who don’t use Facebook. For example, the percentage of teenagers that use Youtube almost constantly or several times today is 60% while the percentage of teenagers that don’t use Facebook is 67%.

It is important that people implement rules on the amount of screen time teenagers are allowed daily.

raw_comment:
What I noticed was of all the social media platforms shown YouTube had the highest percentage of teens who say they use the platform almost constantly, several times a day, and once a day. For example, 41% of teens say they use YouTube several times a day whereas only 32% use TikTok several times a day.

I wonder if YouTube is used the most because its platform is predominantly longer videos compared to the other platforms which are known for their short-form content. I also wonder why Facebook has such a small percentage of people using its platform. 

This doesn't impact me because I tend to stay away from social media but I don't think this data reflects my community. I constantly see teens on Tik Tok, Snapchat, and Instagram throughout the day. I could stand up from my seat to grab a tissue and see at least three teens on one of those three platforms. If the data was collected in my community I would think the percentage of teens who use TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram constantly would be much higher than in the data shown. 

Do the majority of teens use social media at least once a day?

raw_comment:
I noticed that YouTube is the most used platform, which surprised me at first because I thought many kids my age used TikTok and Snapchat way more, but I realized younger teenagers might use YouTube more. Plus, many people use YouTube for entertainment, school, and occasionally to figure out how to do/fix something. I also noticed Facebook was the least used, which makes sense because not many people in my generation have it due to more attractive newer apps. 
I wonder how much these statistics would change if they polled another age group, like people aged forty to sixty. I also wonder how much these statistics will change in the next five, ten or fifteen years. 
As a high school student and a member of our student senate, I rely on social media to get the word out about many of our events and opportunities. These statistics help me know the best way to reach out to my fellow students, by telling me how likely they are to go on a certain app and see our information. Social media also helps me be more involved in my community, for example on Instagram I can follow our athletics, performing arts, national honor society and so much more, which keeps me actively updated with information and opportunities. Social media also keeps me connected with friends from other schools and family out of state.  My catchy headline would be: How is Our Generation Growing Up With Social Media?

raw_comment: I wonder how the data would change if YouTube was split into multiple categories. Since YouTube can be used for a variety of things (music, movies, tutorials, etc.) it would be interesting to see how much each sub category is used. To me, it would make sense that YouTube is the most used "almost constantly" since the teenager could be listening to music, something they can't do on other platforms. Similarly, YouTube could be used "several times a day" for tutorials and how to videos relating to school or home projects. Because YouTube has such a diverse use, it seems almost unfair to compare it to other social media platforms that have less use among teenagers lives. For example, Facebook. Facebook is used mostly among the older generations. While it can be used as a way of communication and keeping up with people's lives, it can also be used as a marketplace. To teenagers, Facebook is less relevant because there is Snapchat for communication and Instagram for both communication and staying in touch with the world and other's lives.  Teenagers can't buy anything off Facebook, so while it is a unique and nice feature, it is something irrelevant to this age group.

raw_comment:
Screen Takeover

I notice that teens use YouTube and TikTok more often than they use Facebook. Snapchat and Instagram are more common than Facebook, but teens use it less compared to YouTube and TikTok. 

I wonder how teens use YouTube more than they use TikTok, Instagram, or Snapchat. I feel as though with apps like TikTok, teens do not utilize YouTube as much as they did before. 

This relates to me and my community because I am a teen myself and have many friends around my age that use social media. Mostly all of my friends use YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat. I use these apps too, mainly TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat. Occasionally I'll watch a video on YouTube. However, I do not use Facebook.

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that YouTube is the most used social media platform while Facebook is the least used. I notice that there is a high percentage of people who don’t use these social media platforms at all, which is an interesting perspective to me as someone who sees all the teens around me on most of the social media platforms. 

2. I wonder what would happen to the data if the sample size went from about 1000 to 10,000 because taking a relatively small sample size in proportion to the total population of teens and increasing it will allow for more data and possibly different results. 

3. This relates to me because I am among the many that do not use any social media platforms other than YouTube and the number of teens that don't have social media surprises me quite a bit. For my community, this shows how widespread and preventive social media use is in teenagers even though some don’t use social media due to its widespreadness whatever negative effects that it has on the mental health of teens will also likely be far-reaching as a result. 

4. “Screens and Teens”

raw_comment:
What do I notice?

Facebook is by far the least-used social media site among teens. Even though TikTok is the most recent app, it is in second place across all five apps. Even though fewer people have Snapchat than Instagram, the people who do have it spend more of their time on it (15% use it almost constantly vs 10% with Instagram). Almost every teenager uses YouTube, which makes sense because it has many applications, like education, long-form entertainment, and short-form entertainment.

What do I wonder?

What does "almost constantly" mean? Does that mean you are using the app every waking hour of your day? Since this was a voluntary survey, how much voluntary response/non-response bias is there? I wonder what the teens who use Facebook use it for? (I know some people who advertise their babysitting/tutoring so parents can see it and don't use it for socializing necessarily.) 

How does this affect my community?

It is clear that many teens spend a large amount of their free time behind a screen, which has been proven to be detrimental to mental health. I also spend a lot of time watching YouTube and on Instagram, so it is interesting to see how many people my age spend even more time online than I do. I think in some ways social media can be a beneficial use of your time, so I think that we as teenagers need to be more aware of when we are just wasting time versus if we are using our time wisely.

"Screenagers by the Numbers"

raw_comment:
This graph shows how often teens say they use each platform. It shows 5 apps in order from least to most used. I noticed Youtube is the most used app. 19% of teens use it almost constantly and 41% several times a day. There's a significant amount of people who use it about once a day or less often. It can be concluded that most teens use Youtube daily. Sometimes schools assign Youtube videos for educational purposes. I use Youtube a few times a week for school. TikTok is mostly either used a lot or not at all. This is  because 9% of teens use it once a day and only 9% of teens use ti less often. This shows the addictive nature of TikTok as most teens either use it all of the time or not at all. The same concept applies to Snapchat. As a Snapchat user, I can say that you feel pressured to respond to friends’ snaps which makes you want to check your Snap right away when you get a notification. With Instagram, slightly more teens said that they used it once a day or less often. However, most people still either use Instagram a lot or not at all. Recently, Instagram has become more addictive as it has adopted Instagram reels which are a similar concept to TikTok. Finally, the majority of people do not use Facebook. I feel like this is pretty common because Facebook is a more adult-dominant app. Overall, this is relevant to me because this survey proves just how addictive social media can be and therefore implies the negative effects it will have on our brains. 
“App Adicttions”

I noticed that Youtube is the most used app.

Most teens use Youtube daily.
Schools sometimes assign Youtube videos for educational purposes.

TikTok is mostly either used a lot or not at all.

However, most people still either use Instagram a lot or not at all.
Recently, Instagram has become more addictive.
Instagram has adopted Instagram reels.
Instagram reels are a similar concept to TikTok.
Finally, the majority of people do not use Facebook.
I feel like this is pretty common because Facebook is a more adult-dominant app.
This survey proves just how addictive social media can be.
This survey implies the negative effects that social media will have on our brains.

raw_comment:
Thanks to all the students who responded.   Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  “Is Social Media the New Addiction?” by Justin of Eagle Crest High School in Aurora, Colo., "The Shocking Usage Statistics Behind Today's Social Media Platforms" by Imran of Valley Stream North High School in Franklin Square, N.Y., “Screenagers: How Teens Today Spend Their Time on Social Media” by Luke of McCall High School in Idaho, “Social Media Obsession: Which Platform Reigns Supreme Amongst Teens” by Santiago of Perth Amboy High School in N.J., “Social Media and the Battle for Teens' Attention” by Ms. Lasky’s AP Language at Middleton High School in Wis. and "Is YouTube the New Facebook?" by Sylvia of Pewaukee High School in Wis.

It is interesting how many commenters were surprised that YouTube and not TikTok was in first place!

Please return on Friday when we will reveal the free link to the article that includes these graphs.  Also in the Reveal are a summary of the topic, additional questions, shout outs for some of the best headlines and Stat Nuggets -- definitions of words that relate to the graph and where you can find them in the graphs.

The next graph will be released by Friday, December 8 and live-moderated on Wednesday, December 13.  The topic – Santa’s wages.

Signing off – Sharon Hessney from Boston, who regularly uses only two of these platforms – guess which ones, and Corey Andreasen from The Hague, The Netherlands, who just wants it to stop raining!

raw_comment:
I notice that YouTube is, by far, the most used social media platform by teens. Only 5% of teens don't use it, whereas apps like Facebook have 67% of teens not using the app at all. It shows how different apps' users differ in usage, as we know that younger generations are using TikTok and YouTube, and it's really only older generations now that may be using Facebook.

I wonder what a graph might look like for short-form content usage specifically. A graph that shows how much teens use apps like TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Instagram Reels would be interesting to see as most of the media consumed by teens today is in that short-form.

This graph relates to me because I am a part of the group surveyed. Teens my age who use different social media apps will all have similar habits in which apps they use based on what is most popular, and this graph also shows how bad some of those teens can be addicted. I wouldn't say I'm "almost constantly" on any app, but the people who gave that answer may be the people who suffer the most from addiction to social media.

This graph shows what social media platforms are being used by teens today and how much they're being used, so my own title for the graph would be "How much of a teen's day is spent on social media?"

raw_comment:
This graph shows how often teens use social media platforms during the day. Youtube is the most used, and Facebook is the least. I notice that the two apps with the lowest "less often" and "about once a day" columns are TikTok and Snapchat. This makes sense because both apps are commonly used to take up time, so it is not unusual for teens to use them several times a day. I also notice that Facebook is the least used, and this makes sense because Facebook is one of the oldest platforms, used mostly by the older generations of Millennials, Gen X, and Baby Boomers. Because I don't notice friends or people around me using Youtube a lot, I wonder if these statistics were taken from ALL use on every platform. I wonder if a lot of teenagers watch Youtube so much because of educational videos for school, and less for "fun"/non-school related videos. This relates to me and my community because most of these platforms consist of short, quick videos and pictures. I have seen statistics that videos and pictures like these lower my generation's attention span, and I wonder what our future will be like if we can only keep out attention on something for 10 seconds or less. 
"Teenagers & Social Media"

What do you notice?

This relates to myself and my community as I am a teenager, and I frequently use 3/5 social medias pictured on the graph. 

Social Surplus

raw_comment:
The graph depicts the preferred social media platforms of teenagers aged 13 to 17. I found it interesting that the three most popular platforms chosen by students were video platforms rather than snapchat, instagram, and facebook, which typically show pictures. I'm curious why only 32% of Tennagers reported using Tiktok while 41% reported using YouTube multiple times a day. Youtube videos are typically more time consuming and longer than a short 15 second to minute tiktok video, so I was surprised that it was used more frequently.  This is important to me and my community because I am a teen growing up in a generation where everyone is addicted to and consumes social media on a daily basis. I think it's interesting to see how teens in my own age groups feel about social media.

The graph depicts the preferred social media platforms of teenagers aged 13 to 17. I found it interesting that the three most popular platforms chosen by students were video platforms rather than snapchat, instagram, and facebook, which typically show pictures. I wonder why only 32% of Tennagers reported using Tiktok while 41% reported using YouTube multiple times a day. Youtube videos are typically more time consuming and longer than a short 15 second to minute tiktok video, so I was surprised that it was used more frequently.  This is important to me and my community because I am a teen growing up in a generation where everyone is addicted to and consumes social media on a daily basis. I think it's interesting to see how teens in my own age groups feel about social media.

raw_comment:
One thing I've noticed when it comes to teens is how drastically online apps change everyday life. Socialization is easier but harder. Hanging out with friends usually end up in some sort of "device break" where nobody talks to another, and just goes on their phones. 

I wonder what would happen to attention spans in the future. With shorter videos like Tiktok, people are used to scrolling and/or going through tons of content in a short amount of time. 

This can relate to me and my friends. When we hangout, they are constantly either watching videos or texting someone like their parents or other friends. I usually don't use my phone around people, as that's proper manners. 

This graph shows the amount of people that use social media, whether teens or adults. i think a catchy headline would be "Let's rethink the 'social' in media!"

What do you notice? 
         I notice that teens tend to use youtube more than tik tok which I kind of find hard to believe. I think that teens have shorter attention spans and would rather watch more short videos that have different topics than a longer one on the same topic. 
What do you wonder? 
         I wonder if it was a mix of teens or was it kind of a common group of teens. If it was more of a common group then they might have similar interests. 
How does this relate to you and your community?

As we use so much of it I feel like we are missing out on some more important things than just watching and scrolling on your phone all of the time an in every "free time" you have.

raw_comment:
What I notice is how youtube is the most constantly used by teenagers and facebook is the least used. Facebook isn't very shocking since more adults tend to use that app, but I was very surprised to see that youtube is the most used app. I expected it to be either Tik Tok or Instagram. What I wonder is how will social media affect our generation in the long run? Will brain power be the same as the current working adults? Social media has many risks to it and has been a very big problem for sources of online bullying as well. What is going on in this graph is it is trying to show how many teenagers truly spend their time using social media daily and additionally, converting it into statistics to make people more aware of it. Multiple times a day, teenagers, myself included, mindlessly scroll through different apps for our own enjoyment, without thinking about the consequences. We need to come to terms with some of the unhealthy side effects it can have when we are older. This relates to my community because since I am in high school, I am surrounded by pretty much only teenagers and we are all addicted to our phones and checking social media constantly, without even realizing it. These statistics could help to encourage teenagers to take a step back and realize how much time is spent on platforms such as these.

raw_comment:
The graph displays/measures how often teenagers say they use or do not use social media platforms. I notice how TikTok is second under YouTube and that teenagers say they almost constantly use TikTok at 16%. I wonder why YouTube is the most used social media platform because I grew out of that phase, but I guess others have not. I also wonder if this affects teenagers' brains and mental/physical health since it seems that most of a teen's time is spent on social media rather than activities or hobbies. This graph shows how much teenagers use social media pretty much 24/7 every day of the week. The screen-time itself can be damaging to one's brain cells and stimulate them which can cause a lack of sleep in many teens. Also, the risks of cyber-bullying, kidnapping, sex trafficking, depression, anxiety, and suicide rates are proven to stem from social media. There are benefits as teenagers can connect/communicate with friends and family, get a new cookie recipe, or watch a TV show. It depends on the person you talk to to get their take on social media. This affects me and my community because as I have mentioned before I am a teenager who uses all of these social media apps, except for YouTube and Facebook, and sees the positive and negative effects. I wish I wouldn't waste time scrolling on TikTok aimlessly instead of doing my GOPO graph but I'm just a teenage girl. 
Super Catchy Title: "I'm Just A Teenage Girl"

raw_comment:
This graph compares how popular social media apps are among teens based on the time spent on them. Teens seem to prefer YouTube and TikTok the most, with almost twenty percent of them saying that they use these apps constantly throughout the day. I notice that these two are video-centric apps, while the less popular apps have a format based more on pictures and text. 
I wonder why Facebook failed and YouTube didn't. They're both some of the oldest social media platforms, so why is one so popular, while the other is losing popularity with the youth? Maybe this is because it's easier to make entertaining content on YouTube. Many YouTubers are household names, but no one knows any famous Facebookers. 
This graph relates heavily to me, because I often find myself hooked on social media. It's an easy way to be entertained for hours. I probably won't stop using TikTok or YouTube, but I should be more aware of how I spend my time on it.

raw_comment:
I notice that YouTube was the most popular platform in 2022. It was used almost constantly by 19% of teens and several times a day by 41% of teens. I also notice that Faceboook was overwhelmingly unpopular with 67% of teens not using it.

I wonder if YouTube and TikTok are more popular because they offer short video reels and a personalized algorithm. I also wonder if young or old teens use one platform more than another, or if there is a platform succession as people age. I also wonder about the average hours of screen time teenagers have in a day.

This relates to me and my community because media consumption is known to have negative effects on people's health, from decreasing one's attention spans to precipitating more extreme opinions. As someone who uses social media relatively frequently, I am curious how these trends will affect the next generation. Will adolescents currently addicted to the internet remain so into adulthood?

My catchy headline: "A New Drug: Technology"

raw_comment:
This graph shows what social media platforms teens from ages 13-17 typically use, and how often. I noticed that up to 20% of these teens are YouTube "almost constantly". I also noticed and expected Facebook to have the least amount of teen users with only around 3% of them using this platform "almost constantly". This data made me wonder what "almost constantly" really means to these teens, and what this means in terms of hours per day. Since this data was also collected in 2022, I wonder if COVID had an impact on this. I also wonder if Spring break impacted these numbers as well. As many teens tend to be on social media on any time off they can get. Today, everyone is almost constantly on their phone. To the point where many people feel as if they couldn't live without it! This is partially concerning as it can make it difficult for people to separate their phone activity from their day to day lives. Although it comes with many benefits and can teach us so much, like simply how to fix something around the house or begin a new hobby. Many young teens abuse these platforms scrolling for hours on end.

raw_comment:
What do I Notice?: I noticed that a lot less teens don't use YouTube compared to other platforms, and a lot of teens do use it. I also noticed that a lot more teens don't use Face Book compared to other platforms. I also noticed that no one checks Face Book compared to other platforms.
What Do I Wonder?: I wonder why less teens use Face Book? Is it because it is primarily an adult platform. Is the content too lengthy for teens? I wonder if the reason Youtube is used more is because it is used by schools to teach at times, and most teens are in required (K-12) schooling. I also wonder why no one checks Facebook consistently?
How Does it Relate to My Community?: This graph relates to my community and I because I myself am a teenager, and I currently am in high school with other teenagers. As well as that, all of me and my schoolmates are generation Z, and are glued to our phones, so it is interesting seeing how we use our time on our phones.

raw_comment:
I noticed that YouTube is the most commonly used by 3% more than the next closest app and that only 5% answered they don't use YouTube. I found it surprising that YouTube was the highest used app. I also noticed that TikTok was only a percentages higher than Snapchat in each society. 

I wonder what would happen to the graph if you changed the age range to 15-17 and 12-14. Different ages use different apps, for example, usually older generations use Facebook as younger generations usually do not. I feel like younger teens tend to YouTube more often. I also wonder how this survey was taken.

As a teen we are surrounded by the pressure of using social media. No one likes to be "out of the loop" so the apps we choose to spend our time on may be because we are needing to fill the standards of society. 

Headline: Is your use of social media consistent with the societal norms of your age group?

raw_comment:
Each social media platform is extremely detrimental and beneficial in different ways. Social media allows for word to get out about relevant news and current events. The detrimental things are though is media manipulation. We don’t absolutely know if this news is true or not. Teens have grown up with social media and it seems that Facebook is becoming more outdated by the day. Over 3/4 don’t use it, maybe due to the “dated” feeling of the platform. YouTube might be questioned as a social media as people can use it as a resource to learn but also learn about current events. TikTok, and instagram are constant scrolling, click through platforms, mind numbing even. Snapchat is more of a communication platform which is surprising to see it has the same usage rates as TikTok and instagram. What I wonder is who almost doesn’t use YouTube, it’s not seen as a “social media” too much and more of just a video platform. And with the recent release of TikTok, compared to the tenured instagram and Snapchat, it still has more overall teens using it than Snapchat and instagram. This definitely makes an impact in my community as so many people use social media as an outlet of stress and entertainment. We are worried though that constant and repeated use will break our minds.

raw_comment: In this graph, it is measuring how often teens use different social media platforms. I noticed that in general, the most commonly used platform out of the 5 was YouTube as the percentages for using it almost constantly at 19% and several times a day at 41% were significantly higher than the percentages in those categories for all the other social media platforms. Additionally, I noticed that Facebook has the greatest percentage of teens not using the platform at all with 67% in that category which is significantly higher than the percentages in the same category for different social media platforms. I also noticed that this graph is for the age range of 13-17 year olds and wonder how the results of this graph would be different for an adult group or group of younger children. I also wonder why YouTube has so much higher usage than something such as Facebook and think it may be due to the types of audiences reached. For example, apps like Facebook categorize a user’s feed based on their networks, but with apps such as YouTube, it is easier for creators to reach a wider audience quickly. This relates to my community because I use social media and it has become almost an essential in society. It is interesting to see how my usage of social media compares to the results of the graph. My headline for this graph would be: “The Apps That Are Consuming Teens’ Time”.

raw_comment:
The graph ranks how often teens use social media platforms. In the graph, I noticed that Youtube is used the most with 19% of teens reporting that it is used “almost constantly” and 41% watching videos “several times a day.” Tik Tok is ranked next with a general 48% of teenagers using the platform pretty frequently. From the data, I noticed that social media platforms that include some form of video were ranked higher on how much time teens spend on the app. This is because YouTube and TikTok are structured on videos (TikTok usually with shorter videos and YouTube with a range of lengths). I wonder what form of media teenagers are viewing most on social media platforms. This is because Youtube can be used for educational purposes as well as for entertainment. Also I am curious because there is a range of interests that can be catered to an individual on social media. Additionally, I wonder  how the amount of time spent on social media ranges for each age (the graph is currently a combination of 13 to 17 year-olds). As a member of generation Z, social media has been a large part of my life growing up. The data relates to my community as social media platforms like YouTube may be heavily used by members of my generation, but then change (like Facebook and Twitter) and newer platforms may be more popular later on. The amount of time my generation spends on social media is also concerning not only because it can hinder brain development. 

Teens Should #Limit Social Media Use

raw_comment:
I notice teens interact, from least to greatest, with YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, Instagram, and Facebook. I notice teens' interaction is the opposite of mine (at 42 years old). I interact the most with Facebook, then Instagram. I don't use TikTok or Snapchat, but also use YouTube some. 

I wonder about the impact on teens' mental health and socialization skills. I remember a case where a Facebook whistleblower testified that Facebook has the algorithms needed ot shelter teens from potentially harmful content, but they don't use it b/c the content benefits them fiscally due to the associated marketing revenue. A Harvard professor who was studying this was recently fired and right afterwards the CEO of Facebook made a large donation to Harvard.https://apnews.com/article/meta-facebook-whistleblower-donovan-haugen-b4716aa988a721dcc1bc651462179f20This relates to me and my community, b/c my bonus daughter is 15 and my students are 18-22. They interact with social media A LOT.

A catchy headline could be "Scrolling Through Generations: Teen Titans of Social Media – Unveiling the Trends in One Graph!"

raw_comment: The graph depicts how regularly teens (aged 13-17) use each social media platform. I notice that the majority of teens utilize some type of social media multiple times per day, with Youtube being the most popular. I am curious about the location of those being surveyed. Were most of the surveyed teens from the United States or elsewhere? Or is it a large range of countries? This would impact the results because if a large percentage of surveyed teens came from regions of extensive poverty, they would not have the technological means to use social media. Additionally, are specific social media platforms more popular in some countries than others? For example, teens using Facebook in the United States is a rarity, but maybe it is popular among teens in Switzerland. This influences my community because numerous studies have been conducted to study the impact of social media, along with technology as a whole. As a large percentage of teens use social media frequently, I think it would be interesting to see a graph of the effects of social media usage. I would title this graph “Teenage Usage of Social Media.”

raw_comment:
I've seen that Facebook has the biggest number of people who don't utilize it, which could be due to its age as well as the platform's outdated style. Compared to the rest of social media, video-focused sites such as YouTube and TikTok are the two most popular among youths, with 19% and 16% of teens continuously using them, respectively.
I'm curious what the typical age of teen Facebook users is, what they use it for, and if teens watch short content on YouTube as they do on TikTok, Instagram, and other platforms, or if YouTube is more commonly used to see lengthier videos.
This relates to me and my community because I looked at my screen time and TikTok was the number one most used app and youtube was the least. My whole community from ages 13-17 have social media and the age tends to go lower every year. Although my most used app was TikTok as a 17 year old, my little sister who is 13 has Youtube as her number one app so it all ranges with the age group.

raw_comment:
P2

For every platform studied, except for YouTube, more teens reported that they don't use the platform more than any other description. For every platform studied, except Facebook, more teens reported using the platform several times a day rather than constantly, about once a day, or less often. YouTube is the most used platform studied and Facebook is the least used platform studied because only 5% of teens do not use YouTube and 67% of teens do not use Facebook. An equal or greater amount of teens reported using EVERY platform studied about once a day or less often in comparison to almost constantly.

Given this, why do most people describe teens as constantly using social media when teens do not report the same? 

This graph is closely related to how I use social media and the ways I see other people my age at school use social media. Most of my day is at school or sleeping. That only leaves so much time for personal obligations, keeping up with friends and family, the gym, reading, or watching television, plus social media. I mostly use YouTube for long periods once a day and only ~3 more platforms for several minutes several times a day.

"How Do Teens Really Use The Most Popular Social Media Platforms?"
