raw_comment:
Youtube is the most used social media app/website across teens, with the majority (41%) using it several times a day. Facebook is the least used, with 67% of teens not using it. Tiktok, Snapchat, and Instagram are very similar in usage, with around 30% of teens using them several times a day.

I wonder why Tiktok media has become so commonly consumed nowadays. Perhaps the short form content is designed to captivate the minds of teenagers and keep them on the app. Why has social media moved so far in this direction? For purely business or money related motives, or because that is the best way to progress forward?

This demonstrates the substantial amount of time that teenagers spend on social media, and that this time could be reshaped into many other priorities in a teenagers life. Though social media works well to socialize, excessive usage isn’t a valuable way of spending teenagers’ abundant time. This impacts both me and the teenagers of the world who participate in social media, as we spend so much of our daily time on these apps.

raw_comment:
This graph illustrates the results of a survey conducted by the Pew Research Center asking how often teenagers (13 to 17) use social media throughout the day. The results show that the majority of teenagers who participated use various platforms at least once a day. While only a low percentage responded that they use these social media platforms constantly, most respondents still report having active accounts. 95% of respondents use YouTube, 77% use TikTok, 59% use Snapchat, and 62% use Instagram. I was quite surprised when I noticed that only 16% of respondents reported constantly using TikTok. I wonder if these results are accurate or if these respondents have succumbed to zombie scrolling and are unaware of how much they use social media. I would respond by saying that I am not a constant social media user. But, according to my Apple screen time report, I used social media for around a total of 30 hours last week. In my community, I see how addicted teenagers around me are to social media. In school, students will step out of class to use the restroom but bring their phones to answer snap chats, DMS, or even just watch a few TikToks before heading back to class. I feel that a lot of people are oblivious to the amount of time they spend on social media throughout the day because it has the effect of engulfing a person causing them to lose a sense of time. 

“Double Tap, Like, and Subscribe: How Much Time Do Teenagers Spend on Social Media?”

1. In this graph I noticed the distribution of the most common social media and how often teens use these platforms from greatest to least. For example, when comparing YouTube to the other platforms, it tends to have a 19% in the category "Almost constantly", the highest percentage compared to the other platforms, and turns out that Facebook is the platform with the least amount of percentage compared to other platforms, as well as we see it has a 67% that don't use the app constantly.

4. Are teens using their time properly? The most used platforms by teens

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that Facebook is the least commonly used platform among teens ages 13 to 17. Younger people tend to think of Facebook as boring and misleading. Therefore, we turn to other social media applications, such as TikTok, which has drastically increased in popularity over the past few years. The graph depicts TikTok as the second most used application following YouTube for first place. 

2. I wonder how social media platforms differ in their utilization of algorithms— rules, and data that determine how content is filtered and recommended to its users, to keep their users addicted. For example, I wonder if FaceBook uses less effective, outdated algorithms because it doesn't appeal as much as YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram toward younger populations. 

3. This graph is relatable to me and my community because we are teenagers, who have not known a life without the internet. Many of us have been exposed to social media at early ages, typically beginning with watching YouTube videos as toddlers. As we have grown older and been given cell phones, the majority of us download social media platforms. There are copious amounts of studies on the benefits and harmful effects of the rise of social media on teenagers. But, this graph serves as a neutral source, which simply informs its audience on how often teenagers ranging from ages 13 to 17 use five major social media platforms.

4.  Is Media Molding Madness?: Statistics Behind Teen's Social Media Platform Usage

## 1) Chart type
- **Horizontal 100% stacked bar chart**

## 2) Layout techniques
- Uses **stacking**: each platform’s bar is divided into usage-frequency segments that sum to 100%.
- Uses **multiple bars by category** (one bar per platform), arranged vertically.
- **No faceting** or small multiples.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Platform (YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, Instagram, Facebook) | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis; one horizontal bar per category; row labels |

| Percentage of teens | Quantitative | Segment length/width along x-axis; percentage text labels inside segments |

- **Title**: “How Often Teens Say They Use Each Platform”
- **Segment labels**: percentages printed inside bars
- **Category labels**: platform names on the left; frequency labels above the bars
raw_comment:
- I notice that Facebook has the highest don't use percentage, which could be from its age, as well as the platform layout not being as modern. This can be supported with sites such as TikTok and YouTube, whose interface is more user-friendly with fewer posts and more videos. Furthermore, I noticed that video-focused sites such as YouTube and TikTok are the two most popular among teens, with 19% and 16% of teens constantly using them, respectively, compared to the rest of social media.
- I wonder how much the substance within these sites contributes to their overall use among teens, with platforms more centered around videos, such as TikTok and Youtube, being higher while more communication-based social media, such as Snapchat and Instagram, are lower in comparison.
- This relates to me and my community, being that social media runs rampant in the lives of my peers and me. Many spend the majority of their day consumed by social media, causing a real problem in the overall productivity of teens' day-to-day lives. I can say this confidently: I am falling victim to wasting away with social media myself. As social media becomes more and more prevalent and a focal point in people's day-to-day lives, it concerns the platform and the content within them being pushed out and affecting teens' lives.
- Social Media Obsession: Which Platform Reigns Supreme Amongst Teens

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I noticed that the most used platform is YouTube, with TikTok being a close second. I also noticed that only 5 percent of teens don’t use YouTube at all. Facebook is the least popular social media platform, with 67% of teenagers not using it at all.  Instagram and Snapchat are respectively 3rd and 4th most popular social media apps. Also, most social media apps are either used several times a day or almost constantly. 

What do you wonder?
What was the sample of teens surveyed for the study and how were the results collected? And would a different sample choice have different results? I also wonder how YouTube maintains this dominance over the social media space. 

How does this relate to you and your community?
It relates to me and my community because social media is a big part of social life among teenagers. Every one of my friends and family use social media and we communicate through it and look at what is happening in each other's life with it. 

Teen’s Social Media Use: How Bad Is Their Scrolling Addiction?

1. What do you notice? If your notice makes a claim, where in the graph is the evidence to support it?

This graph compares 5 different social media platformss and how often teens (ages 13-17) use them. It is demonstrated as bar graphs divided into the percentages of how often they are used. From almost constantly to not always. From the graph we can see that Youtube is the most popular with TikTok close behind and facebook in last, meaning it is used the least. 

2. What do you wonder?

I wonder why the biggest percentages are placed in several times a day rather then almost constantly. And specifically why Youtube is the most popular social media because I personally don't know many people who use it. 

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?

This graph helps me and my peers see where we spend our time and help us reflect on what apps are most popular among our generation. As teenagers we spend a lot of time on our phone and its vital to know what is drawing our attention.

- What are teenagers truly doing on their phones all day? 

- Has your kid been spending more time on his phone then with you? Here's where he's probably spending his time.

Relates to my community as most teens use some form of social media, and this graph shows which social media teens have and use the most.

"The social medias that dominate teens' daily lives"

I wonder what the age range of teenagers is that they surveyed because I think the answers from a 13 year old would drastically vary from the answers of a 19 year old. I think it makes sense that Youtube and TikTok are the most used because they can kind of be a background while you do other things. The high percentage of Youtube being used constantly makes me wonder what types of Youtube videos are being watched, is it more educational or is it entertainment?

raw_comment:
Teens are Addicted to Social Media!

This graph shows the type of social media that teens use the most compared to how often it is used. While examining this graph, we noticed that the most used social media app among teenagers was YouTube. We also noticed that barely any teen uses Facebook, which makes sense because it seems to be targeted towards older groups of people. Also, the “Several times a day” section is the biggest almost consistently for each platform compared to any of the other time stamps.
After analyzing the graph, we started to wonder why YouTube is the most used social media platform among teens. Additionally, we started to wonder what the average age was for teen Facebook users, and what are they using it for. Lastly, we want to know if teens are watching short content on YouTube like they are for TikTok, Instagram, etc, or if YouTube is more commonly used to view longer videos.
This relates to our community because there is hardly anyone in our community that does not use social media, and it was interesting to find out what the most popular platforms were. Social media is very common in our society and this graph shows us how the average teenager spends their time online.

Teen's use of Social Media: Just a Time Sink or a Point of Concern?

In the graph, I noticed that the majority of teens use some kind of social media platform several times a day. Additionally, Facebook is the least used platform by a large margin. This plays into the stereotype I have heard that adults and the elderly make up the majority of people utilizing Facebook as a social media platform. I wonder the results of the same survey given to adults. Another point of interest for me would be comparing social media use in the present to the past couple years and see what platforms were dominant. This relates to me as I am a teen myself as well as my community which has a lot of teens in it. The statement Dr. Vivek Murthy gave is concerning for my community as I have heard much about the mental health effects of social media.

4. Social Media. Good or Bad?

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that YouTube and TikTok were the top two platforms consistently used among teens. This is no shock to me, especially with TikTok, due to its rise in usage during COVID-19.
2. I wonder what social media app developers think when they see how significantly less Facebook and Instagram are used amongst teenagers, considering both applications used to be so popular. I wonder, with the popularity of both TikTok and YouTube, what elements developers specifically take interest in when wanting to create a new app. I also wonder why there is such a huge gap in percentages between TikTok and YouTube concerning teens who don't use the apps.
3. This relates to my community as I am a teenager who also uses most of these social media applications. It’s very interesting to see the usage of certain apps, especially when thinking about how popular apps like Instagram were before TikTok was developed and published. Many teens around me use most of these social media apps, but it does make me question how dependent some teens (including myself) are on social media. Being dependent on social media for whatever reason is never good for one's health, especially their mental health. So, concerns arise.
4. “ The Social Media Shift: The rise of teens use of social media”

|---|---|---|

| Percentage of teens | Quantitative | Segment length/width along x-axis; percentage text labels inside segments |

- **Title**: “How Often Teens Say They Use Each Platform”
- **Segment labels**: percentages printed inside bars
- **Category labels**: platform names on the left; frequency labels above the bars

raw_comment:
I notice that YouTube and TikTok are the top two platforms that are constantly used by teens. 5% of the teens that answered the survey do not use YouTube compared to TikTok which is 33%. 

How many hours did teens who took the survey spend on TikTok compared to YouTube? Which social media platform is most harmful, YouTube or TikTok? Why are Snapchat, Instagram, and Facebook used less? How are teens who use social media frequently affected? What can be done so that these social media platforms can be used for less time or not at all by teens? What would the world be like without social media?

This relates to me and my community as I am a teen in high school. In the hallways at school, I always see teens watching TikTok or videos on YouTube. I do not have any social media apps, so I do not relate the responses in the survey done. However, I do know how addicting all of these social media platforms are. On TikTok, you can keep scrolling and the videos never end. Next thing you know, you have been on your phone for an hour. An hour of your life wasted. YouTube created this new feature called YouTube Shorts. I am happy that I do not have any social media platforms because I am not negatively affected by phone addiction and spend my time wisely. I love to read and play sports. Imagine a world without social media. Teens would not be addicted to their phones and life would be simpler maybe even more peaceful.

Imagine a World Without Social Media. Would the World Be a Better Place?

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice YouTube is the most used by teens. This I find to be accurate, as I'm currently watching a YouTube video while I write this. Most podcasts are also on YouTube, and it's helpful while I'm working because of how me and the rest of my generation lost our attention spans due to being raised on the internet. If you've ever seen those videos of family guy and ASMR or subway surfers parkour, that's basically how bad our attention spans have gotten. I can't even focus on a family guy episode if there's not someone playing with slime under it.
What do you wonder?
I wonder how fast the internet has gained a hold over children and also cocomelon babies. Cocomelon babies and iPad babies are starting to take over the internet space as well. It also makes me think about how war accelerates scientific discovery. It makes me think about how growing up on the internet with little restriction leads children to mature faster. We're exposed to so much of everything that goes on in our world, and it can become overwhelming. I was 13 reading George Orwell. This can also contribute to the mental health rates of my generation, thought they're commonly attributed to comparing yourself to others.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This very clearly relates to me and my community through the fact we've created an online community beyond the real world or ourselves.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
Youtube is the most used platform by teens, and only 5% of teens that have the app don't use it. Each social media platform has been out for a different amount of time, and Youtube has a wider variety of things that interest teenagers.

What do you wonder?
I wonder if the reason that Facebook is the least commonly used app is because of strict parents or the preferences of young teens. Many parents don't allow their kids to have Facebook or other social media platforms, youtube (specifically youtube kids) would most likely be the first social media platform they allow their kids to have, because they have a better job controlling what their kids see. On Facebook, parents have less control, and many people that post on the app are adults.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because most or all teenagers have social media, or should be getting introduced to it. Many teenagers will have limitations on what they are aloud to have on their phone, and they will use the platforms that meet up to their interests.

"Social Media takes over! Will parents put limitations to your phone use?"

raw_comment:
'Social Media is Taking Over Teens' Minds. How did this happen?'

We noticed:
From April 14th to May 4th, 2022, a survey took place for teenagers asking how often they use social media platforms. When the results came back, YouTube had many teenagers using it over other platforms. It had the highest percentage who used it constantly, several times a day, once a day, or least often. The next most popular platform was TikTok, a newer platform in the US since 2018, and it is still rising in popularity. Other popular apps like Snapchat and Instagram didn't have nearly the same numbers as YouTube in each category, but Facebook was the one that fell short the most with 67% of teens not using it.

Our wonder:
What makes these apps much more familiar among teenagers than apps like Facebook and Twitter, which are also fairly popular?

Our relation:
As teenagers, we might use some of the apps in this list and know what it's like to use them all day or throughout the day.
Teenagers might know better than adults about why these apps are so entertaining, considering we use them so much.

raw_comment:
1) I noticed that teens use YouTube and TikTok the most and Facebook the least.

2) I wonder why Facebook is not as engaging to teens as other social media apps when they all share similar elements. Facebook has tons of videos like YouTube and an endless scroll feature like TikTok. What is it about these apps that makes them different from the rest?  I think that the reason why people my age don't use Facebook is because of the age demographic. Facebook is more catered to older people, while YouTube and TikTok are accessible to all ages 13+. Also, YouTube and TikTok offer more diverse content than Facebook does and are more easy to navigate.

3) This relates to me and my community because I'm a teen and I use both YouTube and TikTok pretty often. My generation was the first to grow up with the Internet and social media has become our preferred method of socialization. Throughout the years, social media has proven to have both positive and negative effects, though its negative effects are  troubling and are detrimental to our future if not remedied. 

4) The Age of Social Media

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that most teens seem to enjoy video sharing apps like YouTube and TikTok more than more traditional social media like Instagram and Facebook. This is shown in the fact that YouTube had the highest rate of usage among teenagers, 19% of the surveyed teens almost constantly using it, 41% use it several times a day, 17% use it once a day, 18% use it less often, and only 5% never use YouTube. On the other side of the spectrum Facebook is the least popular platform, with 3% of teens using it almost constantly, 8% using it several times a day, 8% using it about once a day, 14% using it less often and 67%  never use it.
2. I wonder if how many users on a platform depends on the forms of content available on it and the quality of that content. I also wonder if there are any reasons in particular that Facebook has little popularity among the youth and it that statistic was affected by how the data for the study was gathered.
3. This relates to me and my community because this graph shows the rates of usage different platforms have among people in my age group. It displays what people my age are interested in and believe is worth their time to actively consume. 
4. What Content Are Your Teens Consuming And Where?

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that Tiktok and Snapchat have almost the same stats when it comes to percentages of usage, for example for every single category they are both within three percent of each other. Also, when you compare them to Youtube, both apps don't compare to the total amount of usage that Youtube claims to have. I also noticed that they used the age ranges of 13-17 in order to make sure it was strictly teens being examined.

2. I wonder if they asked a variety of teens, did they ask only athletes, only theater teens, or even only teens that aren't involved in anything. I wonder where they got the percentages from and how they were able to calculate the percentages. Also why they would even include Facebook in these stats as its scene as the "older" version of social media and they didn't use some more popular apps when it comes to teens like Reddit or Twitter.

3. This relates to me and my community as I myself use social media for a great portion of the day. With a total screen time of 10 hours and 30 minutes, with a large portion of that being because of Tiktok, and Instagram, I am able to relate to this graph as it truly brings to light how much us teens really do spend on social media. This also relates to my community because it shows where people can be able to interact with each other, and where you can share different aspects of each others lives in order for everyone else to see.

4. Continue To Swipe or Talk Face To Face, Where Have Our Priorities Gone?

About 35% of teens spend their time on YouTube and TikTok compared to the 33% that use Instagram, Snapchat, or Facebook which shows that YouTube and TikTok are the more popular options.

I wonder what factors contribute to teens favorable use of different social media platforms. All social media platforms have similar viewable content so it's interesting why certain platforms are more successful than others. Age groups may play a factor as Facebook is more popular among adults than teens while TikTok is more for the younger generation. 

This relates to me and my community because social media is a huge factor in society. Social media is the new norm of communication as schools and business are even converting to social media to convey information to society. This also relates to me as the graph reflects my own screen time as TikTok and YouTube are my top two most used apps in this past week.

Is Social Media Making Us Less Social?
